title: The moon inside
hook: after a hard shift, a moon over the parking lot and Kabir's line: the moon shines in my body
tomorrow: they fought over Kabir's body. what was under the sheet?

segments.voice: Yesterday's doha: I went looking for the bad one and found none worse than me. Look inside first. Today, Kabir looks inside and finds something else entirely.

A patient yelled at Zoe across the clinic desk today, over a referral that wasn't her fault. She kept her voice steady until the shift ended. Then she sat on Ray's porch steps while the moon came up over the parking lot. Ray, who taught philosophy for years, went inside and came back with a worn book of Kabir, open to this line, in Tagore's English: "The moon shines in my body, but my blind eyes cannot see it." Why can't Kabir see it? Because his eyes are busy looking out.
screen: `A PATIENT YELLS.` → `RAY'S PORCH, A RISING MOON.` → `THE MOON SHINES IN MY BODY.` → `BLIND EYES LOOK OUT.`

segments.voice: The song goes on: the moon is within me, and so is the sun. Kabir isn't boasting about himself. He's saying what's in every body, and he says it plainest in a hymn kept in the Sikh scripture, the Guru Granth Sahib, in the morning raga called Prabhati. In the first, he sings, God made the light, the noor, and from that light came all people. From one light the whole world welled up. So who is good, and who is bad? Don't be fooled, he tells his listeners. That's the teaching: one light in every body. It runs under Kabir's refusal to rank people by caste or by Hindu and Muslim, and the Sikh scripture keeps this hymn among the Gurus' own. Now bring it back to the desk. Kabir doesn't say the man who yelled behaved well. He says the same light is in him, even when his eyes, and Zoe's, are too blind to see it. That's harder than calming down. Zoe can still ask him to stop shouting. By Kabir's hymn, she just doesn't get to decide he's empty inside. The moon over the parking lot doesn't choose whom it shines on, and Kabir says the one inside doesn't either.
screen: `THE MOON WITHIN, AND THE SUN.` · `FROM ONE LIGHT, ALL PEOPLE.` · `SO WHO IS GOOD, AND WHO IS BAD?` · `THE SAME LIGHT IN THE ONE WHO YELLED.` · then, large: `THE MOON INSIDE.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and let them rest from looking out. Notice what's behind the lids: dark, a faint glow, a drifting shape. Don't hunt for a moon; just stay with what's there, and let the breath come and go on its own.
The moon inside: Kabir's picture of the light in every body, there even when the eyes are too busy to see it.
For the road: the moon inside. In the man at the desk too. Five days with the weaver.

howItsDone: Sikhs sing Kabir's hymn of one light ('first, God made the light') in kirtan from the Guru Granth Sahib; in the sant tradition, turning attention inward to the light and sound within is a form of meditation.
